news.snippet: # AI M&A in 2026: Who Is Acquiring Whom. Yet within that more cautious market, A...
news.raw_snippet: # AI M&A in 2026: Who Is Acquiring Whom. Yet within that more cautious market, AI-driven acquisitions have kept moving at a pace and at valuations that outstrip nearly everything else on the board. The result is a bifurcated landscape where discipline reigns almost everywhere except where artificial intelligence is involved, and where the definition of what actually counts as a compelling AI target has narrowed considerably since the freewheeling years of 2022 through 2025. Global M&A value reached roughly $1.6 trillion in the first half of 2026, up about 28% from the same period a year earlier, according to **Boston Consulting Group**’s **Jens Kengelbach**, **Daniel Friedman**, and **Dominik Degen**. That gap is not a contradiction so much as a description of where the market actually stands: buyers are pouring capital into AI-adjacent assets while remaining deeply skeptical of the broader software business models that AI is disrupting.

news.title: AI Investments - by George Serafeim - The Edge
news.snippet: Next semester at Harvard Business School, we will teach a new case on the AI inf...
news.raw_snippet: Next semester at Harvard Business School, we will teach a new case on the AI infrastructure boom that I wrote with my colleague Aliya Korganbekova titled “**Circular AI Deals: Strategic Flywheel or Fragile Stack?**”. It is about helping students connect accounting, financial statements, strategy, capital allocation, and valuation in a consequential setting where the right answer is not obvious. The AI boom is not just a story about models, chips, or data centers. One of the most revealing facts in the case is that Microsoft and Amazon made investments in frontier AI labs that looked strategically similar but showed up very differently in their financial statements. Microsoft invested heavily in OpenAI and reported losses tied to that investment. Amazon invested heavily in Anthropic and reported gains tied to that investment. Or are they creating a fragile stack, where capital, revenue, valuation, and future commitments reinforce one another before the underlying economics are fully visible?

The deal represents the Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Partnership’s first investment, as it joins Global Infrastructure Partners and UAE tech investment firm MGX in acquiring the company. *   BlackRock’s Global Infrastructure Partners, United Arab Emirates-based technology investment firm MGX and buyers under the umbrella of the Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Partnership have closed an acquisition of data center developer Aligned Data Centers valued at $40 billion. BlackRock CEO Larry Fink — who also serves as chair of the AI Infrastructure Partnership — said in the release announcing the deal last year that the investment in Aligned Data Centers will “further [the group’s] goal of delivering the infrastructure necessary to power the future of AI, while offering our clients attractive opportunities to participate in its growth.”.

news.raw_snippet: A Guide to the OpenAI CEO’s Career. From Stanford dropout and Y Combinator president to OpenAI CEO, Sam Altman helped ignite the generative AI boom. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has become one of the AI industry’s most influential figures since bringing the technology into the mainstream with the launch of ChatGPT in 2022. With his casual dress and sociable demeanor, he has appeared on countless media outlets, conference stages and legislative hearings to promote his optimistic vision for the ways AI can usher in a new age of innovation, productivity and abundance — while also warning that it has the potential to eliminate jobs and be used in harmful ways. Sam Altman is the CEO of OpenAI and one of the most influential figures in artificial intelligence. After dropping out of Stanford to launch startup Loopt, he became president of Y Combinator before leading OpenAI and bringing generative AI into the mainstream with ChatGPT.

news.title: This Startup Wants to Buy a Company Just to See What an AI CEO Does With It
news.snippet: # This Startup Wants to Buy a Company Just to See What an AI CEO Does With It. T...
news.raw_snippet: # This Startup Wants to Buy a Company Just to See What an AI CEO Does With It. The startup's founders say they first tested their AI with RollerCoaster Tycoon. One startup is now working on an AI CEO that it hopes could automate an entire business from end to end. Skyfall AI came out of stealth this week after spending the past year developing AI systems that are designed to make the long-term decisions typically handled by company executives. Now, the startup wants to put its technology to the test in the real world by buying a small SaaS or e-commerce business for up to $1 million and letting its AI run much of the company. “Skyfall builds AI agents that can run a company on their own, and we’re proving it by buying software businesses to operate ourselves,” the company’s website reads.
